# M2-1b: Authorization server port

- Milestone: M2
- Branch / worktree: `t/M2-1b`, `../YNAB_AutoCategorizer.wt/M2-1b`
- Depends on: M2-1a
- Touches (exclusive while running): auth/, go.mod, go.sum
- Plan refs: §4 Auth, N7, N9. Spike: `spikes/mcp/{authserver,consent,google,allowlist,revocation}.go`, `server_test.go`,
  `docs/build/spikes/mcp.md`, `docs/build/spikes/mcp-review.md`.
- YNAB access: none
- Deploy: no

## Goal
Port the spike's authorization server into `auth/` on the M2-1a storage, as an `http.Handler` plus a token verifier that
`mcp/` can use, without changing its security properties.

## Scope
- fosite v0.49.0 AS: DCR (not CIMD), PKCE S256 only, opaque HMAC access tokens, introspection, refresh rotation, RFC 7009.
- Google sign-in through go-oidc, allowlist on verified email only, CSRF-protected consent page, pending-login cap 100.
- Subject `u_<sha256(email)[:12]>` mapped to a display name for N9 attribution.
- `RevokeUser(user)` by token generation, with no restart needed.
- Build on the M2-1a API (see the Result in `tasks/M2-1a.md`): `HMACSecret` for `GlobalSecret`, `NewSession` at sign-in, `RegisterClient` and `ClientName` for DCR and consent (`ErrTooManyClients` is the cap refusal). Sessions must be `*fosite.DefaultSession`. Keep the spike's access and refresh lifespans set, because a session with no expiry is refused.
- Port the spike's tests. Close the spike's review lows that apply to this code.

## Out of scope
- Wiring into `serve`, `finbot revoke`, config, the listener and scheduling `Prune` (M2-2).
- Real Google calls in tests: use a fake OIDC provider.

## Acceptance (each must be demonstrably checked)
- [ ] Ported end-to-end test: DCR, authorize, fake Google, consent, code, token, refresh, revoke.
- [ ] Test: unverified email, a non-allowlisted email, a missing PKCE or plain-PKCE request, and a bad consent CSRF token
      are each rejected.
- [ ] Test: a restart (new handler on the same DB) keeps an issued token and its DCR client valid.
- [ ] Test: `RevokeUser` rejects that user's access and refresh tokens at once, and a fresh sign-in works.
- [ ] `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` green

## Result
- Status: DONE
- What changed:
  - `auth/server.go`: `Server` (`NewServer(ctx, Config)`), an `http.Handler` for `/oauth/*` and `/.well-known/oauth-*`. fosite v0.49.0 with DCR, S256-only PKCE, opaque HMAC tokens, refresh rotation and RFC 7009, on `HMACSecret`, `RegisterClient` and `ClientName`. Also `VerifyToken` (go-sdk `TokenVerifier`: `UserID` is the subject, `Extra["name"]` the display name), `ResourceMetadataURL` and `RevokeUser(ctx, user)`.
  - `auth/google.go`: `NewGoogleProvider` through go-oidc, behind `IdentityProvider`.
  - `auth/consent.go`: the CSRF-protected consent page. `auth/allowlist.go`: `ParseAllowlist`, `Check`, `UserID`.
  - `auth/server_test.go`, `auth/allowlist_test.go`: the spike's tests, ported. `auth/fakeoidc_test.go`: a fake OIDC provider on the wire (discovery, JWKS, PKCE check, RS256 id_tokens), so the production verifier runs in every flow test.
  - `go.mod`, `go.sum`: go-oidc v3.21.0, go-sdk v1.8.0, oauth2 v0.14.0 → v0.37.0 (now direct), all as in the spike. `go mod tidy` moved the directive from `go 1.26` to `go 1.26.0`.
- Acceptance:
  - End-to-end DCR, authorize, fake Google, consent, code, token, refresh, revoke → pass: `go test ./auth -run TestEndToEnd`
  - Unverified email, non-allowlisted email, missing or plain PKCE, bad consent CSRF are each rejected → pass: `go test ./auth -run 'TestRejectedSignIns|TestAuthorizeRejectsBadRequestsLocally|TestConsentCSRFAndDecision'`
  - Restart (new handler, database closed and reopened) keeps an issued token and its DCR client valid → pass: `go test ./auth -run TestRestartKeepsTokensAndClient`
  - `RevokeUser` rejects that user's access and refresh tokens at once, and a fresh sign-in works → pass: `go test ./auth -run 'TestRevokeUser'`
  - `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./...` → pass. `go test -race -count=1 ./auth` → pass, run before the last change, which only edits the package comment.
  - Mutation check: 33 mutations of the security checks and related behavior in the new code. 29 failed tests and 4 survived, all of them one layer of a two-layer check. The `CheckSession` calls in `VerifyToken` and `handleToken` survive because storage already enforces the generation. `DisableRefreshTokenValidation` and the `tu != fosite.AccessToken` check each survive alone because the other covers it; turning off both is caught by `TestOnlyAccessTokensAreBearerTokens`. So those second layers have no test of their own.
  - Not exercised: real Google. No test or live run has touched it, so the first real sign-in is M2-5.
- Deviations from brief (all stricter than the spike unless noted):
  - Display name comes from Google's `name` claim, as in the spike. There is no `users` table yet, so the architecture's subject-to-name mapping in `users` isn't built here.
  - The generation is read at the Google callback rather than at approval, and consent re-checks it, so a revoke while the consent page is open applies to that sign-in. New test: `TestRevokeDuringConsent`.
  - `client_name` is cut to 100 runes, so a long name can't push the redirect host off the consent page.
  - The client id is no longer logged (the spike logged it), and the callback no longer reflects Google's `error` parameter.
  - A client evicted during sign-in gets a local 400 instead of a consent page with "(unnamed app)".
  - DCR at the cap returns 503 `temporarily_unavailable` (the spike returned 400 `invalid_client_metadata`). Storage errors return a generic 500.
  - `NewServer` refuses an issuer that isn't a bare https origin, or http on loopback.
  - The token endpoint comes from OIDC discovery rather than `golang.org/x/oauth2/google`, with `AuthStyleInParams` set to match. Discovery and exchange have a 10 s HTTP timeout.
  - `ResourceName` is `finbot` here, since `auth/` owns the metadata handler.
  - Spike review lows: r1-4 fail-closed generation is in `CheckSession` from M2-1a and r2-3 is ported. The rest belong to later tasks: r1-4 HTTP timeouts and shared MCP server, r3-1 DNS-rebinding (M2-2), the M0-2b deploy lows (M2-5).
- Follow-ups for backlog:
  - M2-2: mount with `mux.Handle("/oauth/", srv)` and `mux.Handle("/.well-known/", srv)`. Set `RequireBearerTokenOptions.Scopes` to `[]string{auth.ScopeMCP}`, because `VerifyToken` doesn't check scope itself. The spike's `cors` and `logRequests` middleware in `spikes/mcp/main.go` aren't in `auth/`; browser clients need `cors`, and it isn't named in the M2-2 brief.
  - M2-2 `ResourceName` test can reuse the check in `TestDiscoveryMetadata`, which already asserts `finbot` at the `auth/` level.
  - M2-5: first real Google sign-in, for the discovery-based endpoint.
  - Later: subject-to-display-name from a `users` table, once one exists (the wife's real sign-in is still open in the plan).
- Docs follow-ups:
  - CLAUDE.md: extend the `auth/` package role from the M2-1a follow-up to cover the server, and list `go-oidc` and go-sdk.
